subject: Performance SLO benchmark methodology - exchange
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Erin O'Connell <erin@edgefin.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Performance/SLO benchmark methodology - follow-up

Hi Erin —

Thanks for taking the time today — great to learn more about EdgeFin's latency and streaming needs. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we run the benchmark: 

Recap from the call:
- Target SLOs you mentioned: p95 <= 120ms, p99 <= 200ms for token-latency on your standard credit-card-parsing prompt set.
- Expected concurrency: steady 50 RPS with spiky peaks up to ~75 concurrent streams during market open.
- Throughput requirement: sustain ~6k tokens/sec across pooled hosts during peak.
- Streaming: partial-token streaming required (client shows partial results while inference continues).

What we'll validate in the benchmark:
1) Latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) end-to-end (including networking and small decode overhead).
2) Throughput under sustained and burst traffic patterns.
3) Concurrency behavior and tail latency with KV cache warm vs cold.
4) Streaming correctness and partial-token latency.

Attachments I'm sharing: edgefin_prompt_set_v1.csv (your sanitized prompt samples you agreed to share), redwood_benchmark_harness_v2.zip (our harness — load generator, measurement scripts), measurement_definitions.md (how we compute p50/p95/p99, retry handling, and reproducibility notes).

Proposed next steps:
- You confirm the prompt set attached is the one you want used (or send an updated CSV).
- Confirm the canonical SLO targets above (p99 200ms, p95 120ms) or provide updated numbers.
- Redwood runs an initial benchmark in our staging cluster next week; we will record raw traces and share the harness + results.
- Align on test window (we recommend an early-morning slot to replicate peak pattern with minimal production overlap).

Questions for you before we run:
- Do you need TLS+mutual auth verification during the test (yes/no)?
- Any geo restriction (test only in us-west)?

If that looks right I'll coordinate with Rishi and Vivek to schedule an engineering slot.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap and for packaging the harness. A few clarifications from our side: 

- SLOs: p95 120ms / p99 200ms are the targets we'd like to validate. If we see sustained p99 > 200ms we'll need to understand tradeoffs (quantization vs latency).
- Streaming: yes, partial-token streaming is required — we stream the top-1 token as soon as it's available. Please make sure your harness can measure partial-token latencies separately from full-response latencies.
- Concurrency: the 75 spike is accurate for market open; for the benchmark please include both a steady-state 50 RPS run (30 min) and a 10-min burst run that peaks at 75 concurrency with a 2x arrival-rate ramp.
- TLS/mTLS: we require TLS only for the first pass; if the harness supports mTLS that's great but not required for the initial run.
- Region: us-west preferred.

We attached a tiny supplemental prompt set (10 examples) to test streaming behavior; I'll upload that to the Drive link you included.

Can you also include a short reproducibility checklist for us to run locally if we want to reproduce results? We'd like to be able to re-run with our infra later.

Happy to book Tuesday morning next week for the run — what times work for you?

Thanks,
Erin
Head of Platform Engineering
EdgeFin
erin@edgefin.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 11:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Performance/SLO benchmark methodology - follow-up

Thanks Erin — this is perfect and aligns with what we intended. Per your asks I've added a short reproducibility checklist into measurement_definitions.md (see summary below). Also calling out a few measurement definitions so we're explicit: 

Measurement summary:
- p50/p95/p99: computed on end-to-end response latency measured at the Redwood load generator after TCP+TLS handshake; we report both decode-latency (first byte / streaming first-token) and full-response latency.
- Streaming partial-token latency: time between request start and first-token-delivered event at the client-facing socket. We'll plot CDFs for both first-token and completion.
- Throughput: tokens/sec observed at the client aggregated across hosts; we will also report per-host burn rate.
- Concurrency handling: we will run with cold caches (restart runtime between runs) and warm caches (pre-warm with 10k tokens) and report differences.
- Reproducibility: seed values for randomized batching in harness are recorded; harness is Dockerized (see redwood_benchmark_harness_v2.zip). To reproduce, run the harness with the attached prompt CSV, set --seed=42, and set --streaming-enabled flag to measure first-token latencies. Raw traces and CPU/GPU utilization logs will be uploaded to the Drive folder.

I attached the updated measurement_definitions.md and the harness. For the test window we can do Tuesday 2026-11-24 07:00–10:00 PT — please confirm. We'll reserve a dedicated engineering slot (Vivek and Rishi on-call).

Also, Samir — if you can confirm the supplemental 10-row prompt set is in the Drive link, we'll incorporate it as "streaming_smoke.csv" for the streaming-specific runs.

Next steps:
- Erin: confirm test window (2026-11-24 07:00–10:00 PT) and whether you'd like mTLS on the second run.
- EdgeFin: confirm any data-retention constraints for logs we upload.
- Redwood: we'll schedule the engineering slot and share the run playbook + replay instructions so you can reproduce internally.

Thanks —
Marissa
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
